title: Hot Water Tank Below Brew Temperature
shortDescription: Tank temperature has not reached brew-ready threshold (typically 200F).
fullDescription:
Bunn commercial brewers (ITCB, Axiom, CWTF, Single SH) maintain a continuously heated hot water tank at approximately 200F (93C). If the tank drops below the ready setpoint, the brewer displays Tank Low Temp and blocks brew until the water recovers.

Most common causes are a tripped high-limit, a scaled heating element, a failed heating contactor, or a failed tank probe.

fixSteps.title: Check incoming water
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm water supply open, inline filter not clogged.

fixSteps.title: Reset high-limit
fixSteps.instruction: Access back panel, press manual-reset button on tank high-limit.

fixSteps.title: Descale tank
fixSteps.instruction: Run Bunn descaler per service manual.

fixSteps.title: Test element
fixSteps.instruction: Measure element resistance; replace if open.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — 120/208V element work and tank plumbing.
videoSearchQuery: Bunn Tank Low Temp brewer fix

faq.a: Monthly in hard water; every 3 months with filtered water.

title: Heater Timeout
shortDescription: Heater ran longer than allowed without reaching temperature.
fullDescription:
Heater Time is Bunn's runaway-prevention — if the heater has been commanded ON for more than the allowed time (typically 15-30 minutes continuous) without temperature rising to target, the brewer disables heating to protect the tank and element.

Usually indicates scale, under-voltage supply, or a failed element on one leg.

fixSteps.title: Check supply voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure L1-L2 with brewer running; must meet spec plate.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: Protects against runaway if a contactor welds on.

title: Brew Cycle Too Long
shortDescription: Brew took longer than programmed maximum — low flow through sprayhead.
fullDescription: Bunn brewers time how long it takes to dispense the brew volume. If the cycle exceeds the maximum (typically 8-12 minutes), Brew Time Long is logged. Usually a scaled or clogged sprayhead, clogged dip tube, or failed dump valve.

fixSteps.title: Clean sprayhead
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and soak in descaler, use sprayhead tool to clear jets.

fixSteps.title: Descale tank and tubing
fixSteps.instruction: Run full descale per service bulletin.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech if the dump valve fails.
videoSearchQuery: Bunn Brew Time Long sprayhead descale

faq.a: Bunn specifies their descaler — vinegar can leave residue.

title: Brew Cycle Too Short
shortDescription: Brew dispensed faster than programmed minimum — flow too high.
fullDescription: Brew Time Short means the brewer counted its pulses/flow-meter events faster than expected — dump valve stuck open, flow meter failed, or incorrect brew volume setting.

fixSteps.title: Verify brew volume
fixSteps.instruction: Check programmed brew volume vs desired.

fixSteps.title: Test flow meter
fixSteps.instruction: Per manual, compare pulses vs dispensed ml.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: Too much water for the grounds weight.

title: Refill Timeout — Tank Not Filling
shortDescription: Tank refill did not reach level within allowed time.
fullDescription: Refill timeout happens when the tank level sensor does not see water refill within the fill-timeout window after a brew. Usually a water supply issue — closed valve, clogged filter, frozen line, or a failed fill solenoid.

fixSteps.title: Check supply
fixSteps.instruction: Verify valve open; replace water filter if overdue.

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage at solenoid coil during fill.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech for solenoid work.

faq.a: Every 3-6 months or per cartridge rating.

title: Tank Temperature Probe Failure
shortDescription: Tank probe reading invalid — open or shorted.
fullDescription: Probe fault disables the heater because the brewer can no longer verify tank temperature. Wet electronics or a cracked probe tip are common.

fixSteps.title: Access tank head
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cover; find probe with brass body threaded into tank.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace
fixSteps.instruction: Ohm probe; replace if open or drifted.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: Use fresh tape when reinstalling the probe body.

title: Tank Overflow Detected
shortDescription: Tank water level rose above overflow probe.
fullDescription: Overflow means tank water climbed above the overflow electrode — typically a failed fill solenoid stuck open, or a bad level probe. The brewer disables the fill circuit.

fixSteps.title: Power off, close supply
fixSteps.instruction: Immediately shut water supply and power.

fixSteps.title: Inspect solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Check fill solenoid for debris holding it open.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: No — power off immediately to avoid electrical hazard.

title: Sprayhead Service Reminder
shortDescription: Scheduled reminder to clean or replace the sprayhead.
fullDescription: Not strictly an error — the brewer tracks brew count and prompts sprayhead service on schedule. Dismissible, but skipping leads to Brew Time Long.

fixSteps.title: Reset counter
fixSteps.instruction: Per service menu, reset sprayhead counter.

faq.a: Yes but not recommended — extraction quality degrades.

title: Cleaning / Descale Reminder
fullDescription: Clean prompts the operator to run the scheduled cleaning cycle. Skipping will lead to Tank Low Temp or Heater Time faults.

fixSteps.title: Run clean cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Follow on-screen prompts with OEM descaler.

faq.a: Bunn or a food-safe citric-based descaler — not muriatic.

title: Flow Rate Out of Range
shortDescription: Brew flow rate higher or lower than programmed pulse threshold.
fullDescription: On flow-meter equipped brewers (ITCB, Axiom), Flow Rate fault indicates the pulses/second outside the window — combining with Brew Time Short/Long. Flow meter issues or pressure changes trigger it.
whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.
videoSearchQuery: Bunn flow rate fault clean meter

faq.a: Yes — over 80 psi supply benefits from a regulator.

title: Water Leak Detected
shortDescription: Drip-tray sensor or base sensor detects water.
fullDescription: Some Bunn Smart models include a leak sensor in the base. Leak disables brewing to prevent damage. Causes: failed plumbing seal, overflow event, or over-filled drip tray.

fixSteps.title: Inspect plumbing
fixSteps.instruction: Find and fix leak at solenoid or dump valve.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech.

faq.a: Not recommended — it's cheap insurance against flooding.

title: Generic Brew Cycle Failure
fullDescription: Brew Fail is a catch-all when a cycle did not complete — could be caused by lost power mid-cycle, a door/bin switch opening, or an unclassified fault.

fixSteps.title: Retry and observe
fixSteps.instruction: Press brew; if it aborts at the same point, note message.

fixSteps.title: Check funnel switch
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure funnel fully seated; replace switch if faulty.

faq.a: Yes — discard partial brew since extraction may be uneven.
